given: a sprint-1 stock row whose inventory_code leading segment differs from the row's canonical location column value
when: the up migration runs and backfills batch_number and serial_number
then: the row's location column is unchanged and remains the canonical location; the code's leading segment is not treated as authoritative and does not overwrite location

independence.rationale: AC1 and AC2 concern only batch/serial values; AC3 concerns the location column being left untouched. A migration could correctly split batch/serial yet wrongly overwrite location from the code's first segment, so this outcome breaks independently.

architectural_notes: Infra layer: up revision on the shared branch, read back via app/repositories. Realizes PI2 (UNIQUE(sku, location) from F1 preserved) and NFR-F6-sku-location-unique: the backfill must ignore the code's leading segment and never write location, keeping location canonical and the composite key intact. Owner modules: migrations/versions/* (must not touch location), stock table (UNIQUE(sku, location) unchanged), app/repositories (read-back). Verified by a kind:behavior real-branch test seeding a row whose code leading segment diverges from location; the constraint-survival assertion is the PI2 real-branch test. Shared-branch UP state only.
